football_evidence.question: Can UCLA win at the line of scrimmage?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward UCLA, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.4 of the 2.3 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When UCLA has the ball (big plays through the air): UCLA’s offense turns 16.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Michigan State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 12.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When Michigan State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Michigan State’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.9% of its dropbacks, and UCLA’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Michigan State has the ball (third down): Michigan State’s offense converts 38.6% of its third downs, and UCLA’s defense allows opponents to convert 23.8% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).

When Michigan State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Michigan State’s offense turns 2.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and UCLA’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
contradicting: When UCLA has the ball (big plays on the ground): UCLA’s offense turns 7.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Michigan State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.4% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
quarterbacks: Nico Iamaleava has completed 71 of 116 passes (61.2%) for 978 yards, 8.4 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in five games for UCLA, and has been sacked on 7 of 123 dropbacks.
Ty Dieffenbach has completed 25 of 39 passes (64.1%) for 307 yards, 7.9 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in two games for UCLA, and has been sacked on 2 of 41 dropbacks.

Alessio Milivojevic has completed 118 of 182 passes (64.8%) for 1,270 yards, 7.0 yards per attempt, 7 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in seven games for Michigan State, and has been sacked on 18 of 200 dropbacks.

model: UCLA’s defense has to come out ahead at the line of scrimmage: it stops 21.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line, against an offense that is stopped at or behind the line on 14.6% of its runs.
UCLA’s offense has to hold its own on long runs against a defense that gives up explosive gains on 4.4% of opponent runs.
UCLA’s defense has to come out ahead in the pass-rush matchup: it sacks the quarterback on 5.9% of opponent dropbacks, against an offense that has allowed a sack on 9.9% of its dropbacks.
UCLA’s defense has to come out ahead on long runs: it gives up explosive gains on 3.5% of opponent runs, against an offense that turns 2.2% of its runs into explosive gains.
market: Michigan State’s defense has to come out ahead on long runs: it gives up explosive gains on 4.4% of opponent runs, against an offense that turns 7.3% of its runs into explosive gains.
Michigan State’s offense has to keep winning at the line of scrimmage: it is stopped at or behind the line on 14.6% of its runs, and UCLA’s defense stops 21.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line.
Milivojevic keeps producing at his season rate (64.8% completions, 7.0 yards per attempt, 7 TD, 3 INT).
